(2) fn_largest_remainder SQL function (created by migration 20260718000005_TransactionAllocations) and the transaction_allocations table it targets have ZERO application-code readers/writers (grep confirms only migration files + rebuild-*-canonical-form-order specs reference transaction_allocations by name, no service/controller). (3) This is not an oversight to silently wire up: docs/backend-v2/gap-resolution/canonical-gap-register.json GAP-0009 records an explicit Product Owner decision (REMOVE_SECOND_ACCOUNTING_LAYER, PO-VERIFY-027) that FORMALLY REJECTS transaction_allocations/financial_transactions/financial_accounts as any future path -- 'transactions remains the single canonical financial ledger; there will be no second ledger.' Wiring largestRemainder()/fn_largest_remainder() into transaction_allocations would directly contradict a recorded PO decision. (4) Separately, FinancialRulesService.evaluateRules() (apps/api/src/modules/financial-rules/financial-rules.service.ts) IS wired end-to-end at the event layer (called from transaction/invoice/contract event handlers, emits FINANCIAL_RULE_TRIGGERED, consumed by notification.handler.ts) -- contradicting the map's literal claim of 'no listener' -- but the consumption is COSMETIC: notification.handler.ts only renders 'Regra financeira disparada: {ruleName}', it never reads/applies payload.result.computed (the actual penalty/interest amount) anywhere; no transaction/adjustment is ever created from a triggered rule. findings.summary: CODEBASE_MAP Gotcha #13 CONFIRMED, is a live production bug (not dead code both ends): the 'integrations-sync' BullMQ queue (QUEUE_NAMES.INTEGRATIONS_SYNC) has zero registered @Processor (queue.module.ts's processors provider list has EmailProcessor/NotificationsProcessor/AIJobsProcessor/ExternalDataProcessor/MarketingPublishingProcessor/ArtistPlatformSyncProcessor/MarketBenchmarkRefreshProcessor -- no IntegrationsSyncProcessor, confirmed via grep for @Processor(QUEUE_NAMES.INTEGRATIONS_SYNC) across all processor files: zero matches), but WorkflowQueueService.enqueueOnboardingCheck() and enqueueWorkflowFollowup() (the only two producers targeting this queue) ARE called from real production code paths: apps/api/src/modules/artists/handlers/artist-workflow.handler.ts:144 (artist onboarding) and apps/api/src/modules/contracts/handlers/contract-workflow.handler.ts:139,204 (contract workflow follow-up), both real @OnEvent domain-event handlers wired to actual contract/artist lifecycle events. Every job enqueued via these two real call sites is silently and permanently unprocessed -- BullMQ 'waiting' jobs have no processor to pick them up, ever. Blast radius: (1) functional -- artist onboarding checks and contract workflow follow-ups never actually execute, silently, no error surfaced anywhere; (2) operational -- the queue's 'waiting' jobs have no TTL/removeOnComplete-equivalent (removeOnComplete/removeOnFail only apply to jobs that reach a terminal state, which these never do), so the queue grows unboundedly in Redis for as long as the app runs.
findings.justification: S19=DEPENDENTE_DECISAO_DE_PRODUTO | Semantics only: what onboarding-check / workflow-followup / distribution-sync / spotify:sync should do is undefined; the sole design doc (docs/product-tasks/task-queue-processors.md) contradicts the actual producers. Decision needed: define each job's behavior (then register a real processor and remove it from UNCONSUMED_QUEUE_JOBS) or retire the producers. The operational defect (unbounded growth + false completion) is split into find-queue-containment and CORRIGIDO in commit 671d334. (runtime enum has no S19 value; DIVIDA_ACEITA is the runtime-schema carrier only).

This is a HONEST, correctly-fail-closed placeholder, not a landmine -- confirmed not a bug, just an unimplemented real ad-platform integration (needs per-platform OAuth/API credentials + adapter, e.g. Instagram/TikTok/Facebook Graph APIs) that this audit cannot build without those credentials.

findings.summary: CODEBASE_MAP Gotcha #10 (dead stub entity/repository pairs) CONFIRMED across at least 24 modules (ai, audit-log, auth, billing, briefings, campaigns, clients, content-detections, contracts, ecad-reports, events, health, invoices, integrations, lead-interactions, leads, notifications, phonograms, releases, shares, support-tickets, transactions, uploads, users, works -- full list per repositories-tenant-isolation.spec.ts's own import list). Verified for 3 sample pairs (transactions/leads/invoices): each module-local *.entity.ts is imported ONLY by its sibling *.repository.ts, never registered in database.module.ts's real entity list (all real entities centralize in apps/api/src/database/entities.ts per this repo's documented convention), and neither entity nor repository is ever provided/injected in any real @Module providers array -- confirmed dead at runtime. However, unlike a simple abandoned-file situation, an entire dedicated spec file (repositories-tenant-isolation.spec.ts) exists that imports and unit-tests all ~24 pairs' tenant-scoping behavior in isolation -- meaning this is either (a) deliberate defense-in-depth scaffolding kept 'just in case' a future module adopts the repository pattern, or (b) momentum-driven dead code that even accrued its own test suite. Blast radius of a wrong guess here is real: deleting these files would also require touching/removing this shared cross-module spec, which is a broader, riskier change than a same-pass incidental cleanup should attempt.

findings.summary: CODEBASE_MAP Gotcha #18 CONFIRMED with full end-to-end trace, still real: immediately after creating a release, LancamentoFormModal.tsx's onSubmit unconditionally issues a second PATCH forcing status:'distributed' + metadata.distributedAt/distributionCompletedAt (lines ~918-933), then toasts 'Lancamento criado e distribuido!'. Backend: releases.service.ts emits RELEASE_DISTRIBUTED on this status transition; its only consumer, release-events.handler.ts::onReleaseDistributed, is a genuine empty no-op (tenantId guard only, no body). There is no distributor API call anywhere in this path -- every release in the system is persisted with status='distributed' the instant it is created, unconditionally, and the DB row itself (not just a UI label) misrepresents this. This is a real data-integrity defect, not a cosmetic-only issue like the already-fixed disclosure-class Gotchas (#16/#17/#19/#26): the persisted status value itself is false, so a pure UI disclosure fix would not resolve it. Not changed in this pass: removing the auto-flip or introducing a distinct 'pending_distribution' status is a real behavior/data-model change whose full consumer blast radius (release-list filters, KPIs, any other code branching on status='distributed') was not exhaustively vetted within this cluster's time budget, and forcing it through without that verification risks a worse regression than the current known-bad state.
findings.justification: S19=CORRIGIDO | commit=17e635f | Root cause proven: create persists DRAFT (workflow initialState); form forced PATCH to distributed which the workflow always rejected (only SCHEDULED->DISTRIBUTED exists) -> 400 after successful create; second incompatible consumer: lossy edit status round-trip (distributed/archived/assets_pending/null) -> undefined transition 400 on any metadata edit. Earlier claim that the DB row was persisted as distributed was WRONG and is corrected here: the PATCH was rejected in-transaction, so no data affected, no backfill. Fix: no status PATCH/fake metadata/auto 100% share on create; form never writes status (workflow is the single writer). Consumers reaudited: KPI buckets, display map, notification label, stats endpoint compatible. Tests: releases.workflow.spec, releases.service.spec, web guard + 12 round-trip cases; evid-f258e94f, evid-44d974d7, typecheck/lint/build evid-b2ebf857/evid-8ab2a93d/evid-e556a28c/evid-2c087296.

findings.summary: Sensitive uploads persisted as permanent public URLs: createPresignedUpload returns publicUrl=R2_PUBLIC_URL/tenants/<tenant>/<category>/<uuidv4>/<file>; useUploadToR2/FileUpload store it on entities for documents category too (LeadFormModal lead documents, ContractFormModal files, RH employee documents, ArtistFormModal documents, invoice PaymentSection proofs). Keys are unguessable (uuidv4) so not enumerable. The secure path already exists: GET /uploads/:fileId/download (tenant-checked, 1h signed URL) and /raw.
